walkthrough:
Factorise the leading coefficient $9$ from the first two terms:
$$9x^2 - 36x + 8 = 9(x^2 - 4x) + 8$$

Complete the square inside the bracket:
$$x^2 - 4x = (x - 2)^2 - 2^2 = (x - 2)^2 - 4$$

Expand and simplify into the required form $p(x + q)^2 + r$:
$$9[(x - 2)^2 - 4] + 8 = 9(x - 2)^2 - 36 + 8 = 9(x - 2)^2 - 28$$

Substitute the completed square form into the equation:
$$9(x - 2)^2 - 28 = k \implies 9(x - 2)^2 = k + 28$$

Since $9(x - 2)^2 \ge 0$ for all real $x$, no real roots exist when the right-hand side is strictly negative:
$$k + 28 < 0 \implies k < -28$$

hints: Take square roots and express $x$ in exact surd form.
walkthrough:
Substitute the completed square form into the equation $9x^2 - 36x + 8 = -15$:
$$9(x - 2)^2 - 28 = -15 \implies 9(x - 2)^2 = 13$$

Divide by $9$ and take the square root of both sides:
$$(x - 2)^2 = \frac{13}{9} \implies x - 2 = \pm\frac{\sqrt{13}}{3}$$
